1.explanation:
To reproduce and update these contrast fixes you need to see the source and configuration for both the OverflowMenu dropdown and the Modal/ComposedModal overlay.

• OverflowMenu/OverflowMenu.mdx – this doc shows how the overflow menu is implemented, including shadow styles and theming examples.
• OverflowMenu/next/ – the “next” folder contains the upcoming version’s stories and code that may be using different tokens or implementation patterns; relevant if the change should apply to v11.
• Modal/Modal.mdx – describes the base Modal component and its overlay logic (color, opacity, layering).
• ComposedModal/ComposedModal.mdx – covers the more commonly used composed modal, including overlay props and examples, so you can adjust the overlay styles here.
• ModalWrapper/__snapshots__/ – contains snapshot tests for the wrapper which include markup and styles of the overlay; useful to verify that your changes propagate correctly and don’t break the layer structure.
1.bug_scenario:
The screenshots show two distinct contrast issues when using the Carbon Dark Themes (G90 and G100):

1. Overflow Menu Shadow: In the overflow menu dropdown (the three-dot “•••” menu on table cells), the box-shadow is currently rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3) on all themes. On G90/G100 these shadows recede into the dark background and provide almost no separation between the menu and the page. The proposal is to raise opacity to 0.7 on G90 and/or 0.8 on G100 (or a uniform 0.8 across both).

2. Page Overlay for Modals: When a ComposedModal or Modal is open, the page overlay sits at #161616, 70% opacity on G90/G100 by default. Against the dark page background this feels too subtle. The request is to switch to a pure black overlay (#000000) at 65% opacity to better mute the underlying page.

Key UI elements involved:
• OverflowMenu component and its dropdown “popover” that uses box-shadow
• Modal or ComposedModal page overlay background
• Dark theme tokens (G90/G100) for shadows and overlays
